mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up our journey through “Penis Politics,” let’s take a step back and really take in what we’ve learned. First, emotional labor—it’s real, it’s draining, and it absolutely deserves to be seen and shared. Change isn’t neat or easy. It’s messy, and it asks us to work with both the people who stand with us, and sometimes, even those who don’t. Media has incredible power—it can either shine a light or cast a shadow. And telling the truth? That’s still one of the bravest things you can do. Remember, intersectionality matters. None of us are truly free until all of us are. And maybe most importantly, the future belongs to leaders who lead with empathy and the spirit of collaboration. This isn’t just a story of struggle—it’s a celebration of the resilience and creativity that sparks when people refuse to settle for the status quo. So if you ever feel up against invisible barriers, know this: you are never alone, and your story truly matters. Changing systems can be slow. It might feel thankless at times, and yes, it can even break your heart. But every small act of courage—every time you set a boundary, speak your truth, or reach out to someone in need—helps move us all a little closer to justice. And here’s what I hope you’ll remember: you don’t have to do it all at once, and you definitely don’t have to do it alone. Find the people who get it, honor your own limits, and trust that even the tiniest acts of resistance can plant seeds for something better. The path ahead might be long, but none of us walk it by ourselves. So keep going—because together, step by step, we’re shaping the future.
